en: The Philippines is an archipelago composed of exactly 7,641 islands, which is 534 more islands than the previously official 1987 count.
Mount Apo is the highest mountain in the Philippines, reaching an elevation of 2,954 meters above sea level in Davao.
The Cagayan River is the longest river in the Philippines, stretching approximately 505 kilometers from the Caraballo Mountains to the Pacific Ocean.
Laguna de Bay is the largest lake in the Philippines, covering a massive surface area of about 911 square kilometers.
The Puerto Princesa Subterranean River features an 8.2-kilometer underground waterway, making it one of the longest navigable underground rivers globally.
Mayon Volcano in Albay has erupted over 50 times in the past 400 years, making it the most active volcano in the country.
The Philippine Trench contains the Galathea Depth, the third deepest oceanic trench in the world, plunging 10,540 meters below sea level.
Palawan is the largest province in the Philippines by land area, covering 14,649 square kilometers in the southwestern part of the country.
The Philippine Eagle, the national bird, has a massive wingspan of up to two meters and stands nearly one meter tall.
The Philippines is politically divided into 17 administrative regions and 81 provinces, spanning three main island groups: Luzon, Visayas, and Mindanao.
The Ifugao Rice Terraces stretch for over 20,000 kilometers, which would reach halfway around the globe if laid end to end.
Baguio City receives an average annual rainfall of about 4,000 millimeters, making it one of the wettest cities in the entire country.
